summary: Maximise profit with unlimited buy/sell transactions (holding at most one share).
mainInsight: Any profit over a period equals the sum of its daily increases, so collect every positive day-to-day difference: capture each upswing, skip each downswing.

cards.answer: Greedy: sum every positive day-to-day price increase. Clue: You may trade as often as you like, so any profit is a sum of daily rises, and taking each rise and skipping each fall is optimal.
keyPoints: You may trade as often as you like, so any profit is a sum of daily rises, and taking each rise and skipping each fall is optimal.
cards.explanation: Profit over any period equals the sum of its daily changes, so collecting only the positive ones is the best possible.

promptVariants: What simple rule gives the maximum profit with unlimited transactions?
How do you capture all upswings?
options: Sum all positive day-to-day price increases
Buy at the global minimum price and sell at the global maximum price
Sell on every single day regardless of the earlier prices
Buy only on the first day and sell on the last day
cards.answer: Sum all positive day-to-day price increases
cards.explanation: A rise from a to c through b equals (b - a) + (c - b), so adding each positive step captures the whole rise.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Buy at the global minimum price and sell: The maximum may come before the minimum and multiple swings are possible.

promptVariants: Why is the sum of positive differences achievable with real transactions?
Is it allowed to buy and sell on the same day?
cards.answer: A consecutive run of increases p0 < p1 < ... < pk can be realised as one buy at p0 and one sell at pk, profit pk - p0 = sum of the daily differences. Each positive step can also be viewed as its own buy/sell pair; same-day buy and sell is allowed and yields the same total.
keyPoints: Daily pairs equal the same profit
cards.explanation: The sum equals the maximum because skipping any positive step loses profit.
A rising series gains 2 on each of three days (6); a falling series has no gain on any day.

incorrectOptionExplanations.3, and 0: That counts the number of gains, not their size.
incorrectOptionExplanations.20, and 0: That is the sum of the prices.
incorrectOptionExplanations.6, and 2: A falling series never gives a positive profit.
